You just named today's job. Now the idea: Pick one. Then you will do the lab.

blocks.heading: Pick one
blocks.body:
A **shared folder**, or **Git** (Git is a history tool for files). Not both by accident.

**Master Files** tell Oxygen which booklet owns the pages, so a rename can update pointers. If you have no Master Files, you fix the pointer by hand and you run completeness.

Two desktops, two copies, two people who both think they are home: that is how a page disappears.

blocks.heading: Do the work
blocks.body:
You just met the idea. Now do the lab: One home for the files.

This lab can fail. Fail when: You claim two homes with no bridge, or completeness still shows a missing file after the rename.

Expected: One home written down. Completeness clean after rename. Failure mode written.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.body: If you picked a folder: rename one topic file, then fix the pointer in the map by hand. Run completeness.

steps.title: Step 4
steps.body: If you picked Git: enable Master Files on the map in Oxygen (verify the label) and rename a topic. Confirm the pointer updates. Run completeness.

steps.body: Write the failure mode of two people editing two copies and both calling their copy the home.

blocks.lead: Answer with words from today only.
blocks.q: Master Files in Oxygen exist to update pointers when you rename a file. True or not?
options: True :  that is the point. Without them, a rename is a silent broken link
Not true :  Master Files publish the PDF
Not true :  rename never breaks a booklet
blocks.why: The booklet stores a path. Rename the file and the path is a lie until something updates it.

blocks.lead: Answer with words from today only.
blocks.q: You and a teammate each have a full copy of kitepump on two desktops, and neither copy is Git. What fails first?
options: One of you overwrites the other’s page, and nobody can say which copy is real
blocks.why: Pick one place the files live. Two homes are how pages vanish.
